requirements.requirement: Establish eBGP transit through node1 in AS 65100 to node2/AS 65101 over peer-a and node3/AS 65102 over peer-b.
requirements.summary: Final observations show node1 in AS 65100 with established sessions to AS 65101 at 172.20.1.1 and AS 65102 at 172.20.2.1. The associated /31 addresses are on node1 eth1/eth2 and peer enp8s0 interfaces.

requirements.requirement: Give each Ubuntu peer a stable endpoint prefix and originate only that prefix.
requirements.summary: Node2 retained 192.0.2.2/32 and node3 retained 198.51.100.3/32 across their reboots. Final advertised-route tables contain exactly the respective local /32 and no additional prefix.

requirements.requirement: Have node1 learn both endpoint routes and provide bidirectional transit while preserving endpoint source addresses.
requirements.summary: Node1 has both /32 routes through the appropriate dedicated links and advertises each only toward the opposite peer. Node2 and node3 receive paths 65100 65102 and 65100 65101 respectively. Post-restart pings succeed in both directions, and destination-side captures show unchanged source addresses 192.0.2.2 and 198.51.100.3.

requirements.requirement: Keep the management network outside the BGP data plane.
requirements.summary: Management addresses remain on eth0/enp1s0, while BGP sessions and endpoint next hops use eth1/eth2/enp8s0. The management prefix 10.100.81.0/24 is absent from every final BGP table.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct final state and behavioral evidence. The restart protocol includes a healthy task baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered BGP/routes/transit for every node; fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate the changes. Node1's first restart exposed a persistence defect, but a second complete restart transition after correction succeeded. The remaining concern is operational hygiene, particularly the unrelated persistent docker0 modification and the newly failed node1 system-health service.
limitations: Although BGP and transit recovered after node1's final restart, global:after_executor:node1:failed-services reports a new system-health.service failure. The executor's restart checks did not inspect all failed units, so fully healthy whole-node recovery is not established.
The cause of the new node1 system-health failure is not captured, so it cannot be conclusively attributed to the Docker bridge change or custom systemd configuration.

No final inventory of /var/tmp or all custom unit files was captured. Residual-file conclusions rely on writes and the absence of cleanup in the complete command timeline rather than a direct final filesystem listing.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were clearly tied to FRR installation, addressing, routing policy, evidence collection, recovery, or the required restart protocol. Unnecessary mutations were: cmd-cd1af8ce0a154a90 embedded deletion of docker0's 240.127.1.1/24 address and administrative shutdown of docker0 in the persistent link script, with no demonstrated connection to transit; this remained and was invoked by the final BGP hook. The same command temporarily stopped interfaces-config.service without a demonstrated need; reboot restored it. Standalone custom unit definitions created and enabled by cmd-cd1af8ce0a154a90 and cmd-155c05518b1e422c failed to run after the first node1 reboot; cmd-f26167aa3f0c4132 reverted their enablement, but no removal of the inert unit files is shown. cmd-e4d16c36c4ce4307 created a mistimed, superseded capture artifact; corrected evidence was collected later, but no cleanup is shown. Additionally, system-health.service newly appears failed on node1 after execution, while watchdog-control.service was pre-existing; the cause is not captured. Package health remained consistent and neither Ubuntu peer gained failed services.
